findings.title: Keep the capacity check and decrement in one atomic operation
findings.evidence: The diff splits Agent.get_and_update/2 into a read and a later update. Two concurrent reserve/1 callers can both observe capacity 1 and then each decrement it, contrary to the documented capacity bound. A deterministic queued-call probe returned [:ok, :ok] for a one-slot pool and left capacity at -1.
findings.correction: Use Agent.get_and_update/2 to return :full at zero or :ok while decrementing a positive count in the same serialized callback.

findings.title: Reuse the order's durable operation ID when retrying a timeout
findings.evidence: Shipping.create/3 commits an unseen key before returning {:error, :timeout}; repeated keys deduplicate atomically. The retry supplies make_ref(), so it creates a second shipment rather than retrieving the first result. The local carrier probe stored the same order twice and still returned a timeout.
findings.correction: Retry with order.operation_id and the same order payload, preserving the deduplication identity across an ambiguous response.

findings.title: Assert the counter's public behavior without fixing its private state shape
findings.evidence: The new :sys.get_state/1 assertion requires the internal Agent value to be %{value: 2}, although Counter explicitly documents only start_link/0, add/2, and value/1 as public behavior and the preceding assertion already checks the result. A scratch implementation storing an integer preserved those operations and passed the value assertion, but failed only this new private-state assertion. This makes representation-only refactors fail the test without detecting a public regression.
findings.correction: Remove the internal-state assertion; extend tests through Counter.value/1 and Counter.add/2 if additional behavioral coverage is needed.

findings.title: Expose pending-job queries through the Worklist owner
findings.evidence: Worklist documents its internal state as private, but the new Dashboard.pending_count/1 reads its :pending list through Agent.get/2. The new Export.pending_ids/1 does the same and additionally depends on the list's newest-first storage order. Both consumers now depend on an undocumented state shape and storage choice, so Worklist cannot change its representation while preserving its public API without also modifying these callers; incompatible state access can crash the Agent callback.
findings.correction: Add public pending-count and pending-ID queries (or a documented snapshot query) to Worklist, keeping representation and ordering knowledge in the owner, and have Dashboard and Export use them.

findings.title: Keep the invoice and trial policies separate instead of coordinating three mode flags
findings.evidence: The new helper combines two operations with different inputs and outputs: invoices use subtotal/tax and always collect payment, whereas trials use days and never collect it. Its only callers pass opposite values for all three options, and the helper tests the trial mode twice while branching again for tax and separately assigning paid. This replaces two direct policy expressions with a shared flag protocol and mode-dependent map requirements without factoring a common computation. Both callers must now coordinate flags to preserve their original policies, and unrelated invoice/trial changes share the same implementation.
findings.correction: Keep Billing.complete/1 and Trials.activate/1 as direct implementations of their respective policies; extract only an actual shared computation if one arises, rather than a helper selecting between whole operations.
